text: Hold eye contact and smile with the barista while you order.
drop: Looking down at your phone or the card reader the whole time.
success: Two seconds of eye contact and a smile. That's it.

text: Ask one stranger for the time.
drop: Opening with a long apology ("so sorry to bother you...").
success: One question asked out loud, answer heard.

text: Say "morning" to a neighbour or someone you pass in Hitchin.
drop: Pretending you haven't seen them.
success: One word, said out loud, while looking at them.

text: Compliment one specific thing on a stranger: their dog, shoes, bag or coat.
drop: Walking off before they can reply.
success: One sentence, then pause long enough for a reply.

text: Stand in a queue for 3 minutes without your phone.
drop: Phone or headphones as a shield.
success: 3 minutes with the phone in your pocket.

text: Thank the bus driver, guard or ticket staff out loud with eye contact.
drop: Mumbling it at the floor.
success: An audible "thanks" with a glance up.

text: Ask the cashier "how's your day going?" and listen to the answer.
drop: Rushing to pack your bag in silence.
success: One question asked, answer listened to.

text: Ask one colleague how their weekend or evening was.
drop: Doing it over Slack/Teams instead of in person or on camera.

text: Keep your camera on and say hello at the start of one call.
drop: Camera off and joining silently.

text: Ring a friend or family member with a quick question instead of texting.
drop: Texting first to check it's OK to call.

text: When someone asks what you'd prefer, say an actual preference.
drop: "I don't mind, whatever you want."

text: On the commute, nod or smile at someone who catches your eye.
drop: Snapping your eyes away instantly.

text: Leave one genuine comment (not an emoji) on a property contact's LinkedIn post.
drop: Rewriting it for ten minutes.
success: One sentence posted within 2 minutes of starting.

text: Offer to make tea or coffee for the people around you.
drop: Waiting for someone else to offer first.

text: Ask the barista a non-order question: a recommendation, or how their day's going.
drop: Pre-scripting the whole exchange in your head.
success: One question asked and the answer listened to.

text: Have a 60-second chat with a shop assistant about a product.
drop: Cutting it short with "just looking, thanks".

text: Introduce yourself to one person at an event or gathering.
drop: Hovering near people you already know.
success: Your name, their name, one question.

text: Send a friend a voice note instead of a text.
drop: Re-recording it until it's perfect.
success: Sent on the first or second take.

text: Ask a colleague one genuine question about their work or interests, then one follow-up.
drop: Steering the conversation back to yourself straight away.

text: Phone a local business with a question instead of using their website.
drop: Scripting every line before dialling.

text: Ask one question out loud in a meeting.
drop: Saving it for a private message afterwards.
success: One question asked in the room or on the call.

text: Ask a stranger for a recommendation: lunch near the office, best coffee near the station.
drop: Opening with a long apology.
success: Question asked, answer heard, thanks said.

text: Point out a wrong order, wrong change or wrong item, politely.
drop: Accepting it to avoid a fuss.
success: The issue said out loud, once.

text: Share a different view on something low-stakes (a film, food, a plan) with a friend or colleague.
drop: Instantly adding "but you're probably right".
success: Different view stated with one reason.

text: Make one remark to someone on the commute (delays, weather) and see if it turns into a chat.
drop: Headphones in, eyes down.
success: One remark out loud. A chat is a bonus.

text: Invite a colleague to grab lunch together.
drop: Asking in a way that's easy to decline ("no worries if not!!").
success: A clear invite made. Their answer doesn't matter.

text: Send a short personal message to one property contact you've met before.
drop: Drafting it for more than ten minutes.

text: Chat for a minute with someone you see regularly but never really talk to (gym, office lobby, neighbour).
drop: Sticking to a nod because it's "easier".

text: Start a conversation with a stranger at a cafe.
drop: Keeping your phone out as an exit plan.

text: Speak first in a meeting: an update, a point or a question.
drop: Waiting for the "right moment".

text: Invite someone you'd like to know better for a coffee.
drop: Hedging the invite until it isn't really one.
success: A clear invite made. Their answer doesn't matter.

text: Give a 2-minute update without notes.
drop: Reading from notes or over-rehearsing beforehand.

text: Cold message one useful LinkedIn contact (agent, investor, sourcer) with a specific ask.
drop: Rewriting it five times.

text: Phone an estate agent about a listing instead of emailing.
drop: Scripting every word.

text: Ask a manager or peer for direct feedback on something you did.
drop: Pre-empting criticism by putting yourself down first.

text: Raise a concern or alternative view in a meeting.
drop: Softening it into a question you don't really mean.

text: Propose a specific group plan (pub, walk, dinner) in a group chat, with a date and time.
drop: Waiting for someone else to organise it.

text: Make a phone call you've been putting off (GP, bank, landlord, tradesperson).
drop: Waiting for the "right time".

text: Ask a shop assistant or bartender for a detailed recommendation and chat for 2+ minutes.
drop: Cutting it short once you've got the answer.

text: Join a group conversation already in progress (event, office kitchen, pub).
drop: Standing on the edge without speaking.

text: At a London event or queue, ask someone what brought them there, then follow up.
drop: Bailing after the first answer.

text: Say no to a request you'd normally accept reluctantly.
drop: Over-explaining and apologising.
success: A clear no, two sentences of reason at most.

text: Host a small table or drinks for three or more people.
drop: Over-planning every topic of conversation.
success: It happens and you did the inviting.

text: Hold a polite disagreement for 5 minutes without giving in just to end it.
drop: Conceding to escape the discomfort.
success: Five minutes. Change your mind only for a real reason.

text: Present to a group of five or more (team meeting, meetup).
drop: Reading slides word for word.
success: Delivered, with eye contact around the room.

text: Open a conversation with a stranger at a property networking event.
drop: Hovering by the drinks or only talking to people you know.

text: Ask for something you might get a no to: a discount, a favour, a better deal term.
drop: Asking in a way designed to be refused.
success: A clear ask made. A no still counts.

text: At an event, introduce yourself to three different people.
drop: Leaving early once you've done one.

text: Cold call a landlord, agent or sourcer about a potential deal.
drop: Reading from a script.

text: Propose an idea to a senior person in person or on a call.
drop: Burying it in a long email instead.

text: Have a 5-minute conversation with a stranger (train, bar, event).
drop: Using your phone as an exit.

text: Invite someone new to a group plan and introduce them around.
drop: Leaving them to fend for themselves.
success: Invited, and introduced to at least two people.

text: Phone to negotiate or complain: a bill, contract or service.
drop: Accepting the first answer.
success: Ask made, plus one follow-up push.

text: Ask a question from the floor at a talk or meetup.
drop: Hoping someone else asks it.

text: When service goes wrong, politely ask for a better fix or for a manager.
drop: Letting it go to avoid friction.

text: Give honest, constructive feedback to a colleague or friend.
drop: Wrapping it in so much praise it disappears.
